reason: From 2.0 s on, the two films are nearly the same frame for frame, so the opening decides. In A's 0 s frame one wide shot holds both hands planted on the keyboard, the small 'Question' card on the clipboard page under the 'Health record' label, and the labelled 'OpenEvidence AI tool' just right of the chart. The send's start point and landing point are both in frame. By 1 s the card has left the page and both hands are still on the keys, so nothing appears or vanishes without cause. The cut at about 2 s to the tool close shows a thin card sliding out under the tool. At 3 s it lies on the desk with empty Sources and Accuracy slots, and at 4 s three teal/teal/orange chips fill Sources. Across s2 to s3, A keeps the same chart, tool and hands in a readable left-to-right layout.
rejected_reason: B's 0 s close at desk height crops the destination tool to 'Ope / AI to' at the right edge, so the send's landing isn't readable in the first frame. At 1 s the camera has pulled back, the card is already gone and the left hand has vanished. The right hand floats raised, palm open, above the desk with no contact with any card, so it reads as a wave, not a push. The same floating raised hand appears at 15 s with the question card above and left of it, again not touching. At 24 to 28 s and 40 to 41 s the caption band covers the answer card's header more than in A. B's larger s2 date-tag detail (8 to 10 s) doesn't make up for these opening problems.
